title: Two tomatoes, one from a Dutch greenhouse and one from a field in Spain. Whic…
caption:
Two tomatoes, one from a Dutch greenhouse and one from a field in Spain. Which one took less water to grow? The greenhouse, by about ten to one. A glasshouse tomato takes 15 to 20 litres a kilogram, with the drainage caught and sent back to the plants. A field tomato in a dry region, flood irrigated, can take 300 to 500. The global average is about 214. The heaviest tomato you buy is the one in a tin, because paste comes from dry fields on pumped water. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-tomato (link in bio). Did you pick the field?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Every chatbot answer, search and stored photo passes through a building full …
caption:
Every chatbot answer, search and stored photo passes through a building full of hot computers, and most of those buildings are cooled by water that leaves as steam. Google reported about 23 billion litres consumed by its data centres in one year, the drinking water of a city of a few hundred thousand people. Your own share depends on the building: almost nothing in a closed loop hall in a cool climate, about half a litre for a long conversation in an evaporative hall in a desert. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-industries-data-centres (link in bio). Did you ask a chatbot something today?

#waterfootprint #industrialwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Flushable wipes are flushable, says the packet. Tested: false. A wipe leaves …
caption:
Flushable wipes are flushable, says the packet. Tested: false. A wipe leaves the bowl, and so would a sock. It is made to stay whole when wet, so it stays whole in the sewer, catches on a joint, and meets cooking fat that hard water turns into a hard soap. That is how a fatberg is built. The one under Whitechapel in 2017 weighed 130 tonnes and took nine weeks to cut out. Britain clears about 300,000 blockages a year, and wipes are in most of them. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/myth-flushable-wipes (link in bio). Do you flush wipes?

#watermyths #drinkingwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Karachi gets about half the water it needs through its pipes. The other half …
caption:
Karachi gets about half the water it needs through its pipes. The other half arrives on trucks. Several thousand tankers fill at hydrants cut into the city's own mains, most of them without permission, and sell the water back to flats, factories and hospitals at ten to twenty times the piped price. The river has enough. A new canal has been on the drawing board since 1990, and eight million people have arrived since the last one was built. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-places-karachi (link in bio). Has a water truck ever come to your street?

#watercrisis #watersecurity #water #thirstyplanet

title: In the 1970s millions of hand pumps were sunk across Bangladesh so villages c…
caption:
In the 1970s millions of hand pumps were sunk across Bangladesh so villages could stop drinking from ponds that carried cholera. Child deaths fell by more than half. The water was free of germs, and it carried arsenic from the mud at levels that poison slowly over decades. Nobody tested for twenty years. The test, when it came, was a strip of paper for a dollar or two. Five million wells were painted green or red, and about 20 million people still drink from red ones. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/plain-water-arsenic (link in bio). Has anyone tested the water you drink?

#watertreatment #wastewater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Potato or rice, which one takes more water to grow? Rice, by about nine to on…
caption:
Potato or rice, which one takes more water to grow? Rice, by about nine to one: 2,500 litres a kilogram against 290. The field drinks about the same either way. The difference is that a hectare of potatoes gives forty tonnes of food and a hectare of wheat gives four to eight. Per calorie the potato still needs a third of the water. A bag of crisps is a thousand litres a kilogram, the same potato with its water fried out. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-potato (link in bio). Rice or potatoes tonight?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: The largest copper mine on Earth sits in the driest desert on Earth, and for …
caption:
The largest copper mine on Earth sits in the driest desert on Earth, and for thirty years it pumped a thousand litres a second from an aquifer the rain had not refilled since the ice age. The springs the villages farmed went dry. In 2020 it stopped. Now it desalinates seawater at the coast and pumps it 3,200 metres up and 180 kilometres inland. The desert's problem became the coast's, because the brine goes into the bays where the fishing villages are. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-industries-copper (link in bio). Would you pay more for copper that drank the sea instead of a village's spring?

#waterfootprint #industrialwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Desalination is the answer, everyone says. Quick guess: if every desalination…
caption:
Desalination is the answer, everyone says. Quick guess: if every desalination plant on Earth ran flat out, what share of the world's fresh water would it make? Under one percent. About 35 cubic kilometres a year against 4,000 used, and seventy percent of that goes to farms that can pay a few cents a cubic metre, against the sea's dollar or more. It is a good last answer for a coastal city, and a poor first one for anyone else. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/myth-desalination-is-the-answer (link in bio). What was your guess?

#watermyths #drinkingwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Cairo drinks the Nile, and the Nile is mostly Ethiopian rain. Ninety seven pe…
caption:
Cairo drinks the Nile, and the Nile is mostly Ethiopian rain. Ninety seven percent of Egypt's water is one river, and 85 percent of that river fell as rain in a country that has just finished the largest dam in Africa across it. In a normal year the same water still arrives. The harder problem is at home. Four fifths of the river goes to farms, and the delta that feeds the country is sinking and salting, because the silt that built it now stays behind Egypt's own dam. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-places-cairo (link in bio). Does your city's water start in another country?

#watercrisis #watersecurity #water #thirstyplanet

title: The part of a desalination plant that keeps it alive is a plastic tank the si…
caption:
The part of a desalination plant that keeps it alive is a plastic tank the size of a fridge. It doses a clear liquid at 2 to 5 milligrams a litre. Without it, the salt the membranes leave behind grows into chalk on the membrane and blocks it. A few milligrams hold back a hundred times their weight in hardness, by sitting on each crystal seed so the next ion finds no place to land. Get the dose right and the membranes last seven years. Get it wrong and they last two. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/plain-water-antiscalants (link in bio). Is your tap water from the sea?

#watertreatment #wastewater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A banana, an apple, an avocado. Which one took the most water to grow? The av…
caption:
A banana, an apple, an avocado. Which one took the most water to grow? The avocado, by a mile: about 400 litres for one, grown in dry country on water from a pipe. A banana is about 100, and nearly all of it rain that fell on a plantation in Ecuador or the Philippines. Every export banana is the same cloned plant, and the fungus that kills it has just reached South America. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-banana (link in bio). Did you guess the avocado?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Palm oil is in about half the packaged products in a supermarket, and it is t…
caption:
Palm oil is in about half the packaged products in a supermarket, and it is the least thirsty vegetable oil there is: about 5,000 litres a kilogram, against 14,500 for olive oil, and nearly all of it rain in the wettest places on Earth. Its water trouble is at the other end. The mills send out water at ninety degrees a hundred times stronger than sewage, and a third of the plantations stand on drained peat that burns every dry season. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-palm-oil (link in bio). Would you boycott it, or buy certified?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A concrete floor the size of a living room took about 3,000 litres of water i…
caption:
A concrete floor the size of a living room took about 3,000 litres of water in the mix, and several times that to cure it and to wash the gravel at the quarry. The world pours thirty billion tonnes of concrete a year and uses about nine percent of all industrial water to do it, mostly in the places building fastest, which are the driest. Every dam, pipe and treatment plant is cast from it. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-industries-concrete (link in bio). What is your floor made of?

#waterfootprint #industrialwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Boiling water removes everything, everyone says. Tested: false. A minute at a…
caption:
Boiling water removes everything, everyone says. Tested: false. A minute at a rolling boil kills every germ that lives in water, including the parasite that made 400,000 people ill in Milwaukee in 1993 and shrugs off chlorine. It removes nothing else. Salt, nitrate, lead and arsenic stay in the pan, a little more concentrated, because some of the water has left as steam. The white scale on your kettle was in the water all along. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/myth-boiling-water (link in bio). Do you boil your tap water?

#watermyths #drinkingwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: In 2008 Barcelona ran its reservoirs down to a fifth and brought drinking wat…
caption:
In 2008 Barcelona ran its reservoirs down to a fifth and brought drinking water in by tanker ship from Marseille. Then it rained, and the desalination plant the city built in answer sat almost idle for ten years. In 2024 the drought came back, longer and deeper, reservoirs at 15 percent, an emergency declared, and this time the plant ran flat out while the city got through on about 100 litres a person a day without the taps going off. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-places-barcelona (link in bio). Could your city live on 100 litres a day?

#watercrisis #watersecurity #water #thirstyplanet

title: At 12:28 on 25 January 2019 a dam above an iron ore mine in Brazil turned to …
caption:
At 12:28 on 25 January 2019 a dam above an iron ore mine in Brazil turned to liquid and a wave of mud ran through the canteen at lunchtime. 270 people died. The dam was holding tailings, the ground rock left after the metal is taken out, and it was built from the same mud it held. There are several thousand dams like it, one fails seriously every year or two, and the old ones above towns will never be made safe. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/plain-water-tailings (link in bio). Is there a mine upstream of your town?

#watertreatment #wastewater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A cotton T shirt or a polyester one, which is better for water? Round one is …
caption:
A cotton T shirt or a polyester one, which is better for water? Round one is not close: cotton needs about 2,700 litres before it reaches the shop, polyester a few dozen. Round two turns it around. Every wash of polyester sheds plastic fibres that no sewage works can destroy, and cotton's fibres rot in weeks. The shirt you wear a hundred times beats both. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-cotton-vs-polyester (link in bio). Which one is in your wardrobe more?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Before a factory makes a tablet, it makes water. Purer than anything you drin…
caption:
Before a factory makes a tablet, it makes water. Purer than anything you drink, kept hot and moving so nothing can grow in it. The problem is the other end. Washing the vessels between batches sends a share of the drug down the drain, and below the antibiotic plants near Hyderabad the lakes have carried more antibiotic than a patient's blood. That is where resistant bacteria are bred. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-industries-pharma (link in bio). Did you know most of the world's antibiotics come from a few industrial districts?

#waterfootprint #industrialwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Everyone says a shower saves water. It did, in 1975, when a shower was a tric…
caption:
Everyone says a shower saves water. It did, in 1975, when a shower was a trickle. A bath is about 80 litres, full stop. A shower is the flow of your head times the minutes you stand there, and a power shower passes the bath at five minutes. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/myth-bath-vs-shower (link in bio). Try it tonight: a bucket under the head for one minute. How many litres did you get?

#watermyths #drinkingwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: India's technology capital sits on a plateau with no river, a hundred kilomet…
caption:
India's technology capital sits on a plateau with no river, a hundred kilometres from the nearest one and 1,400 metres above it. It was built on lakes, drained them, built over them, and pumped the ground beneath until, in the summer of 2024, the wells of half the city ran dry and the tech companies sent their staff home. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-places-bangalore (link in bio). Could your city pump its water up a mountain?

#watercrisis #watersecurity #water #thirstyplanet

title: The water reaching a farm well today fell as rain in the 1990s. It carries th…
caption:
The water reaching a farm well today fell as rain in the 1990s. It carries the fertiliser of that year, the half the crop never used, which sank through the soil and has been travelling sideways ever since. One well in five in Europe's farming regions is over the limit. Denmark cut its losses in half and waited twenty years for the groundwater to turn. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/plain-water-nitrate (link in bio). Would you drink from a well in a maize field?

#watertreatment #wastewater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Building one car takes somewhere between 50,000 and 400,000 litres of water. …
caption:
Building one car takes somewhere between 50,000 and 400,000 litres of water. Nobody can pin it closer, and the spread is the story: steel, aluminium, glass, rubber and the paint shop all have their own water, in different countries. An electric car moves most of that water from the refinery to the mine. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-car (link in bio). Which part of a car would you guess is thirstiest?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: The factories that make the chips in your phone use water like a small city, …
caption:
The factories that make the chips in your phone use water like a small city, about 150,000 cubic metres a day for the largest group of plants in Taiwan, and they need it purer than anything a city drinks. When Taiwan's rain failed in 2021 the island chose its chips over its rice. The new factories are being built in the desert. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-industries-semiconductors (link in bio). Would you have chosen the chips?

#waterfootprint #industrialwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A lawn looks like nature and drinks like a crop. In a hot dry summer a square…
caption:
A lawn looks like nature and drinks like a crop. In a hot dry summer a square metre of green grass takes about 9 litres a week, as much as a square metre of wheat, and grows nothing you can eat. Turf is the largest irrigated crop in the United States, ahead of maize. Las Vegas paid people to dig theirs up and then banned the decorative kind by law. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/myth-lawns (link in bio). What would you put in its place?

#watermyths #drinkingwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Five million people drinking from one enormous dam. In a drought Sydney built…
caption:
Five million people drinking from one enormous dam. In a drought Sydney built a desalination plant, then switched it off when the rain came and left it idle for seven years. The next drought switched it back on, and now they are doubling it. A plant that sits idle for years is doing exactly what it was built for. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-places-sydney (link in bio). Does an insurance policy have to be used to be worth it?

#watercrisis #watersecurity #water #thirstyplanet

title: The water leaving a treatment plant has no lead in it. The lead comes from yo…
caption:
The water leaving a treatment plant has no lead in it. The lead comes from your own pipe, the short one between the street and the kitchen, laid a century ago because lead was soft and cheap. There is no safe level, and the fix is a plumber, not a plant. Flint happened when the water chemistry changed and the pipes started to shed. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/plain-water-lead (link in bio). Do you know what your service pipe is made of?

#watertreatment #wastewater #water #thirstyplanet

title: The lithium in an electric car battery came, most likely, from a salt flat in…
caption:
The lithium in an electric car battery came, most likely, from a salt flat in Chile or Argentina, where brine is pumped up and left in the sun for a year to evaporate. About two million litres of it for one battery. The industry says brine is not water. The villages on the edge of the salt flat, whose springs are drying, say it is. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-battery (link in bio). Is brine water?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: For every barrel of oil pumped out of the ground, about three barrels of salt…
caption:
For every barrel of oil pumped out of the ground, about three barrels of salty water come up with it. It is ancient seawater, too salty for anything, and it goes back underground. In Oklahoma they injected so much of it that the state went from two earthquakes a year to nine hundred. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-industries-oil-and-gas (link in bio). Did you know an oil well is mostly a water well?

#waterfootprint #industrialwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A full dishwasher uses about 10 litres. The same plates washed by hand under …
caption:
A full dishwasher uses about 10 litres. The same plates washed by hand under a running tap use 40 to 100. The machine wins because it reuses the same few litres over and over and only lets them go at the end. It loses only when you rinse everything first or run it half empty. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/myth-dishwasher (link in bio). Do you rinse before you load?

#watermyths #drinkingwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Nairobi has been on water rationing since 2017. The utility supplies about tw…
caption:
Nairobi has been on water rationing since 2017. The utility supplies about two thirds of what the city needs, loses half of that on the way, and the people in the poorest districts pay the most per litre of anyone in the country, from a jerry can. A tunnel under the mountains is meant to close the gap. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-places-nairobi (link in bio). What does a litre of water cost where you live?

#watercrisis #watersecurity #water #thirstyplanet

title: In 1854 a London doctor took the handle off one water pump and the cholera in…
caption:
In 1854 a London doctor took the handle off one water pump and the cholera in the street stopped. That was the moment the world learned that disease travels in water. Every city with a treated supply and a sewer has been free of cholera since. It still kills tens of thousands a year, in the places that have neither. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/plain-water-cholera (link in bio). Did you know a glass of clean water is the most effective medicine ever built?

#watertreatment #wastewater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A litre of sunflower oil carries about 6,000 litres of water, nearly all of i…
caption:
A litre of sunflower oil carries about 6,000 litres of water, nearly all of it rain on the black earth of Ukraine and southern Russia. The war in 2022 showed how much of the world's frying depends on that one region. Olive oil carries more than twice as much; rapeseed, less. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-sunflower-oil (link in bio). Which oil is in your kitchen?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Half the nitrogen in the food on your plate started in an ammonia plant, wher…
caption:
Half the nitrogen in the food on your plate started in an ammonia plant, where natural gas and water are forced together at high pressure. About a tonne of water goes into every tonne of ammonia as an ingredient, and far more as cooling. The world makes 180 million tonnes of it a year. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-industries-ammonia (link in bio). Did you know fertiliser is made partly of water?

#waterfootprint #industrialwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: The jug on your counter mostly takes out one thing: the chlorine that was kee…
caption:
The jug on your counter mostly takes out one thing: the chlorine that was keeping your water safe. Once that is gone, the jug and the warm kitchen do the rest, and after a few days the water in the jug can carry more bacteria than the water from the tap. It is good for taste and for hard water scale. It is not a safety device. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/myth-filter-jugs (link in bio). How old is the cartridge in yours?

#watermyths #drinkingwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Sixteen million people, two continents, and in January 2021 the reservoirs we…
caption:
Sixteen million people, two continents, and in January 2021 the reservoirs were at a fifth. The utility counted 45 days of water left. A city on the sea, between two seas, with not enough fresh water: the pipe from the Melen river was meant to fix that, and took twenty years. The rain came first. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-places-istanbul (link in bio). What would your city do with 45 days?

#watercrisis #watersecurity #water #thirstyplanet

title: Old cities carry rain and sewage in the same pipe. When it rains hard the pip…
caption:
Old cities carry rain and sewage in the same pipe. When it rains hard the pipe cannot hold both, so the mix is let out into the nearest river through an overflow built for exactly that. In England the overflows ran for 3.6 million hours in 2023. The practice is a century old. The monitors that made it visible are new. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/plain-water-storm-overflows (link in bio). Would you swim in your river the day after a storm?

#watertreatment #wastewater #water #thirstyplanet

title: An outdoor cannabis plant in a California summer drinks about 22 litres a day…
caption:
An outdoor cannabis plant in a California summer drinks about 22 litres a day, twice what a grapevine does on the same hillside. Before it was legal, hidden grows in the northern hills took more water from some streams in August than the streams had, and the salmon paid. Indoors, the water problem becomes an electricity problem. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-cannabis (link in bio). Did you expect a plant to drink that much?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: One egg carries about 196 litres of water, and the hen drank almost none of i…
caption:
One egg carries about 196 litres of water, and the hen drank almost none of it. It is in the maize and soy she ate to lay it. That makes the egg one of the better deals in your fridge, and it means where the grain grew matters more than how the hen was kept. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-egg (link in bio). Would you have guessed higher or lower?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Seawater carries 35 grams of salt in every litre. Your tap water carries a fe…
caption:
Seawater carries 35 grams of salt in every litre. Your tap water carries a few hundred milligrams, and that is what you taste, what furs up your kettle, and the part of cleaning water that no filter can see. The industry calls it TDS, total dissolved solids, and it is the most useful number in the business. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/plain-water-tds (link in bio). Does your kettle have scale in it?

#watertreatment #wastewater #water #thirstyplanet

title: One avocado took about 400 litres of water to grow. For most foods a big numb…
caption:
One avocado took about 400 litres of water to grow. For most foods a big number is not bad news, because the water was rain. Not here. Avocados grow in dry places, in Chile, Mexico and Spain, and the water arrives through a pipe from a river or a well that the people nearby needed too. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-avocado (link in bio). Where do yours come from?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Every farmer on Earth is trying to get more water to the crop. Winemakers are…
caption:
Every farmer on Earth is trying to get more water to the crop. Winemakers are the exception: they spend their careers keeping the vine a little thirsty, because a stressed vine makes better grapes. A glass still carries about 109 litres, three times what beer does per litre. The heat is starting to bend the old rule about never watering vines. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-wine (link in bio). Red or white tonight?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A treatment plant does not make dirt disappear. Everything it takes out of th…
caption:
A treatment plant does not make dirt disappear. Everything it takes out of the water ends up in one pile, and that pile is almost all water itself. Dealing with it eats up to half the plant's running costs. The same pile is a fertiliser, a fuel and a headache, depending on the week. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/plain-water-sludge (link in bio). Where do you think it ends up?

#watertreatment #wastewater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Europe's biggest manufacturing sector is food, and most of the water a food f…
caption:
Europe's biggest manufacturing sector is food, and most of the water a food factory uses never touches the food. Between half and two thirds of it goes on cleaning the equipment, every shift, because the next batch must not taste of the last one. The best plants now use the warm washing water to heat the building. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-industries-food (link in bio). Ever seen the inside of a food factory?

#waterfootprint #industrialwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A sheet of office paper carries about 10 litres of water, most of it drunk by…
caption:
A sheet of office paper carries about 10 litres of water, most of it drunk by a tree over the years it grew. The mills that turn the tree into paper have cut their own water tenfold, which makes paper one of industry's quiet successes. The tree is the part nobody can shrink. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-paper (link in bio). How many sheets did you print this week?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Pour a glass of milk down the drain and, by the water industry's own measure,…
caption:
Pour a glass of milk down the drain and, by the water industry's own measure, you have sent something hundreds of times stronger than sewage. The measure is called COD, and it is simply how much oxygen the water would eat as it rots. Every discharge permit in the world is written around that one number. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/plain-water-cod (link in bio). What is the strongest thing that goes down your sink?

#watertreatment #wastewater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A slice of bread carries about 65 litres of water, nearly all of it the wheat…
caption:
A slice of bread carries about 65 litres of water, nearly all of it the wheat. Wheat covers more of the Earth than any other crop and most of it grows on rain. The part that does not is pumped from some of the most overdrawn aquifers in the world. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-bread (link in bio). How many slices did you eat today?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A litre of milk takes about 1,020 litres of water to make, and the cow drinks…
caption:
A litre of milk takes about 1,020 litres of water to make, and the cow drinks almost none of it. It is in the grass and the grain she eats every day. That is also what decides whether dairy or a plant milk is the heavier choice: it depends on the farm behind the carton, not on the label. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-milk (link in bio). Which milk is in your fridge?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: You flush, and the water starts a journey you never see: under every street i…
caption:
You flush, and the water starts a journey you never see: under every street in town, mostly downhill, to a plant on the edge of the city where bacteria eat what you sent them. It takes about a day. The plant runs partly on the gas those bacteria make. Most of the world's flushes never reach a plant at all. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/plain-water-after-you-flush (link in bio). Do you know where yours goes?

#watertreatment #wastewater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Next to almost every serious factory stands a building nobody notices. It is …
caption:
Next to almost every serious factory stands a building nobody notices. It is a treatment plant for the factory's own water, and its biggest cost is air: half or more of its electricity goes to blowing bubbles so the bacteria inside can breathe. Whether the river next door is alive depends on that building. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/plain-water-etp (link in bio). Ever noticed the tanks at the back of a factory?

#watertreatment #wastewater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A flooded paddy looks as if rice grows underwater. It does not. Rice grows in…
caption:
A flooded paddy looks as if rice grows underwater. It does not. Rice grows in wet soil, and the flooding is mostly weed control, a trick thousands of years old. The price of the trick is that rice takes a third of all the irrigation water on Earth, about 2,500 litres a kilogram. Farmers are learning to let the field dry between floods. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-rice (link in bio). Did you know the flood was for the weeds?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Every number in the first month of this series was spent before the product r…
caption:
Every number in the first month of this series was spent before the product reached you, in a field or a factory. Read enough of them and they start to feel like an accusation. They are not. Factory water is concentrated, and concentrated water can be cleaned and used again: 70 to 90 percent of it, in a well run plant. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/the-turn (link in bio). Which number stayed with you?

#water #thirstyplanet

title: A 200 gram steak carries about 3,100 litres of water, and 98 percent of it ne…
caption:
A 200 gram steak carries about 3,100 litres of water, and 98 percent of it never touched the animal. It is three years of feed: grass, hay and grain. Whether that is rain on a hillside or a river in a dry valley depends entirely on the farm. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-beef (link in bio). Do you know how the beef you buy was raised?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A 100 gram bar of chocolate carries about 1,700 litres of water. Per kilogram…
caption:
A 100 gram bar of chocolate carries about 1,700 litres of water. Per kilogram, cocoa outweighs beef. The reason it is less alarming than it sounds: almost all of it is rain on a farm in Ivory Coast or Ghana. Cocoa's real worry is heat, not water. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-chocolate (link in bio). Does the number change how the bar tastes?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: The textile industry takes 93 billion cubic metres of water a year and gives …
caption:
The textile industry takes 93 billion cubic metres of water a year and gives almost all of it back, hot, salty and coloured. The colour is the dangerous part: dye blocks the light, and a river without light has nothing growing in it. The best mills now clean and reuse most of what they take. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-industries-textile (link in bio). Have you ever seen a river the colour of this season's fashion?

#waterfootprint #industrialwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A pair of jeans carries about 8,000 litres of water from the cotton field to …
caption:
A pair of jeans carries about 8,000 litres of water from the cotton field to the shop. The most detailed study ever done on a single garment found something else: a quarter of a pair's lifetime water is spent after you buy it, in your washing machine. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-jeans (link in bio). How often do you wash yours?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: A cotton T shirt carries about 2,700 litres of water, roughly what you drink …
caption:
A cotton T shirt carries about 2,700 litres of water, roughly what you drink in three years. Most of it fell on a cotton field or was pumped onto one. In Central Asia the pumping for cotton was enough to turn the Aral Sea, the fourth largest lake on Earth, into a desert. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-tshirt (link in bio). How many T shirts are in your drawer?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Your cup holds about 125 millilitres. Growing, washing and roasting the beans…
caption:
Your cup holds about 125 millilitres. Growing, washing and roasting the beans in it took about 140 litres, a thousand times more. Most of it was rain on a hillside in Brazil, Vietnam or Ethiopia. The total is the least interesting part; where it fell is the story. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-coffee (link in bio). How many cups today?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: At school we learn that seventy percent of the planet is water. Almost none o…
caption:
At school we learn that seventy percent of the planet is water. Almost none of it is water we can use. Take away the sea, the ice and the deep ground, and the rivers and lakes that supply most of what people use are 0.3 percent of the fresh water on Earth. That small share never runs out, because it keeps raining. Cities run dry anyway. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/the-0-3-percent (link in bio). Did that number surprise you?

#water #thirstyplanet

title: An island with no rivers, no aquifers, and a water supply that came across a …
caption:
An island with no rivers, no aquifers, and a water supply that came across a border from a neighbour. So Singapore decided to make its own, from its own sewage, cleaned until it is purer than rain. The equipment was ordinary. Persuading a whole country to drink the result was the real engineering. It can now cover 40 percent of demand. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-places-singapore (link in bio). Would you drink it?

#watercrisis #watersecurity #water #thirstyplanet

title: A glass of beer carries about 74 litres of water, and almost none of it was s…
caption:
A glass of beer carries about 74 litres of water, and almost none of it was spent at the brewery. It is the barley in the field. Inside the brewery, water mostly goes on cleaning, and brewers watch their litres per litre more closely than almost any industry I know. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/thirsty-beer (link in bio). Would you have guessed the field or the brewery?

#waterfootprint #hiddenwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: In most of Europe, bottled water is not cleaner than tap. It is tested less o…
caption:
In most of Europe, bottled water is not cleaner than tap. It is tested less often, under a different law, and it sits in a warm lorry and a shop window for months before you open it. Tap water is tested every day and carries a little chlorine to protect it on the way to your kitchen. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/myth-bottled-water (link in bio). When was the last time you looked at the date on a bottle of water?

#watermyths #drinkingwater #water #thirstyplanet

title: Wastewater is 99 percent plain water. The word covers your shower drain, the …
caption:
Wastewater is 99 percent plain water. The word covers your shower drain, the outflow of a dye house and the rain off a car park, which is why on its own it tells you nothing. A whole industry exists for the last one percent. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/plain-water-wastewater (link in bio). What do you picture when you hear the word?

#watertreatment #wastewater #water #thirstyplanet

title: You drink about two litres a day. You use about ten thousand. The rest is ins…
caption:
You drink about two litres a day. You use about ten thousand. The rest is inside the coffee, the shirt, the lunch and the phone, spent in fields and factories before any of them reached a shop. I have spent my career inside the water industry, and this page is my attempt to make that water visible. Full story: thirstyplanet.media/articles/the-water-you-cant-see (link in bio). What would you like me to count next?
